what_c40_claimed: 15 of 16 lethality inversions run in the over-optimistic direction -- the engine believing it can KO where the simulator says the defender survives -- and this is the 'premature commits into guaranteed KOs that were not' bias flagged for post-C27 evaluation, still present in the residual support gaps.
verdict: RETRACTED. The asymmetry was an artifact of my own thresholds.
the_error: I compared 'SOME engine branch KOs' (lethal mass > 0%) against 'NO engine branch KOs' (lethal mass = 0%). Those are not mirror conditions -- the first fires on a 1.3% chance, the second requires certainty. Any distribution-valued engine will look over-optimistic under that pairing. The engine enumerates a distribution and the simulator rolls one outcome; a 5% KO branch that did not fire is the engine being right, not wrong.

the_symmetric_test.method: compare the engine's lethal branch MASS against the realized outcome, both sides at the same 50% threshold
the_symmetric_test.significance: one-sided binomial p = 0.109 against a fair split; two-sided ~0.22. Not significant.
the_symmetric_test.brier_score: 0.066 mean over all 74 -- the engine's KO probabilities are well calibrated even on a population selected for unreachability
the_symmetric_test.caveat_stated_honestly: this population is SELECTED on unreachability, so 0.066 is not a calibration estimate for the engine at large; it is only evidence that these 74 rows do not show a lethality-pricing defect

the_mechanism_i_also_misread: Every engine KO branch had delta exactly -hp0 with zero overkill, which I first read as a marginal max-roll overshoot -- a defect damage_calc.rs documents twice in its own comments. It is not. HP clamps at zero, so EVERY KO branch has delta -hp0 by construction. Zero overkill is the representation, not a finding.

what_survives_from_c40.n_hit_KO_threshold_shift: 56 of 74 (75.7%) STANDS -- it is a magnitude claim, not a lethality one, and does not depend on the asymmetric threshold
what_survives_from_c40.so_the_search_term_is_still_nonzero: the engine-gap bucket does change tree pricing, but through n-hit-KO thresholds, not through lethality

corrected_ranked_target_for_objective_4: The 56 n-hit-KO threshold shifts, NOT the '15 inversions'. C40 ranked the 15 first on the strength of the retracted bias claim; with that gone they are 6 rows of ordinary distribution behaviour and should not lead.
does_not_reach_a_pass: no code changed; unattributed stays at 485
